text:
Forgive me,

literary friends,

my dear academic

friends, forgive me.

I did not follow the ‘career’ of a poet.

I merely grew up with this

vocation for gathering meadowlarks,

but I never knew how to tame them.

They are uncultivated, they do not bow.

They are wild,

they do not polish their violins.

They are plain,

they do not deck themselves in borrowed plumes.


So forgive them,

their uneducated song

is living and imperfect.

What can I do?

If I gather words of agony

I do not see whether they sound musical,

and if I find hopes,

I give them away,

however much they may lack

the exact measures.

Then,

leave me like this!

Leave me there, in the streets,

with them, the simple people.

Let Juan, María, and Pedro

repeat my songs,

carry them to market,

take them into the factories,

send them to the lumber camp.

Let them repeat them

now, and while

they need them.

Later, tomorrow, soon,

they will have forgotten them.

And that is all right.

So forgive me.

Forgive me

that in the midst of combat,

in the midst of prisons,

in the midst of beasts that torture,

in the midst of night and its ambush,

in the midst of victims and fear,

in the midst of filth and shame,

in the midst of gunpowder and fire,

in the midst of hunger and lamentation,

and in the midst of this dislocated world,

I sometimes lose the rhythm and do not count

on my fingers

each verse!

There is no remedy for that.

I do not know how to measure blood!

I do not know how to count tears!


I do not know how to rhyme weeping!

translation.title: More Words of Mine
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. Its direct address, colloquial register, and repeated protest against aesthetic measure are retained.
